about: The named business measures plx.sql {measure: ...} answers from (operating/measures.py). Each is one aggregate over one business view: value (an aggregate over the view's own columns), per (the column its value is split by: a money measure's currency or a quantity's unit; values in different currencies or units are never added), date (the column a period is read on; none: a snapshot as it stands now), where (the rows it counts), dimensions (the view's columns it may be broken down by), owner (the team that owns the definition). Every statement is made from these fields only and runs as the reader through the business views' door. A measure may instead name a source: a record type read through the door's records view (operating/measure_sources.py), its columns stated in the entry; its requires lines are read from measured fills (devloop/source-health.json) and a measure too thin for a figure is refused as not_measurable with the fills.

measures.name: Revenue invoiced
measures.definition: Net line revenue on posted sales invoices (item and miscellaneous lines, before tax), by invoice date.
measures.ask: Why did revenue change last month? Which customers drove it?

parameters.says: invoices held only in Business Central

measures.name: Gross margin
measures.definition: Line revenue less line cost on posted sales invoices, by invoice date. Lines without a cost are not counted, nor lines whose cost looks wrong (cost more than 5 times the line's revenue: see cost_looks_wrong). A line whose margin the reader may not read counts in unread_cells.
measures.where: margin_basis IS DISTINCT FROM 'cost_unknown' AND coalesce(NOT (revenue > 0 AND margin < -4 * revenue), true)
measures.ask: What was our gross margin percent each month this year, per currency?

parameters.says: invoices held only in Business Central

measures.name: Units sold
measures.definition: Quantity on item lines of posted sales invoices, by invoice date, per unit of measure.
measures.ask: Which products sold the most units in the last 90 days?

parameters.says: invoices held only in Business Central

measures.name: Sales invoices issued
measures.definition: Sales invoices by invoice date, one per invoice record.
measures.ask: How many invoices did we issue each week this quarter?

parameters.says: invoices held only in Business Central

measures.name: Sales orders booked
measures.definition: Distinct sales orders by order date, every status (a quote is an order type), one per order record.
measures.ask: How many orders did each salesperson book last month against the month before?

parameters.says: orders held only in FileMaker, the Portal or Business Central (no Sage order)

measures.name: Sales order value booked
measures.definition: Value of sales orders (not quotes) by order date.
measures.ask: What will order value booked look like over the next 3 months?

parameters.says: orders held only in FileMaker, the Portal or Business Central (no Sage order)

measures.name: Open sales orders
measures.definition: Sales orders open now (not shipped and invoiced in full, not quotes). Orders held only in FileMaker, the Portal or BC count like any other.
measures.where: status = 'open' AND order_type IS DISTINCT FROM 'quote' AND of_record IS NOT NULL
measures.ask: How many open orders does each customer have right now?

parameters.says: copies of an order of record (same customer and customer PO): the copy is that order

measures.name: Late sales orders
measures.definition: Open sales orders past their required date now, not quotes. Orders held only in FileMaker, the Portal or BC count like any other.
measures.where: status = 'open' AND days_late > 0 AND order_type IS DISTINCT FROM 'quote' AND of_record IS NOT NULL
measures.ask: Which customers have the most late orders right now?

parameters.says: open on the books but not live: nothing left to deliver, or nobody has ordered or invoiced for longer than closed orders take

measures.name: Receivables open, net
measures.definition: What each customer account owes now, net: the sum of every open ledger document on the account. Unpaid invoices count positive; unapplied payments (receipts), prepayments and credit notes on the same account count negative and are part of the balance, not a separate figure. For gross unpaid invoices alone (before credits, receipts and prepayments), use receivables_open_gross. An account whose net is negative is owed money by us. Never net one account against another, even for the same parent company.
measures.ask: How much do customers owe us in each currency, by aging bucket?

measures.name: Receivables open, gross (invoices)
measures.definition: What customers owe now on open invoices alone, gross: unpaid invoices only (unapplied payments/receipts, prepayments and credit notes are not netted). For the net account balance including credits and unapplied payments, use receivables_open.
measures.ask: How much do customers owe us in open invoices (gross, before credits) per currency?

measures.name: Receivables overdue, net
measures.definition: What each customer account owes now on documents past their due date, net: overdue invoices positive, the account's unapplied payments, prepayments and credit notes negative (they carry days_overdue too).
measures.ask: Who should we chase first for overdue payments?

measures.name: Receivables overdue, invoices
measures.definition: What customers owe now on invoices past their due date (credits, receipts and prepayments not netted).
measures.ask: Who should we chase first for overdue payments?

measures.name: Payables open
measures.definition: Amount PLX owes on open Sage AP ledger documents: every payee, not only trade suppliers (card issuers, the tax body, payroll and individuals' expenses are payees too). payee_class says who it is owed to by the GL account Sage posts the vendor's invoices to (default account, or Sage AP distribution set when no single default account is set): trade (inventory and cost of sales suppliers: raw materials, packaging, freight in, product testing), expense (services, freight out, rent, IT, consulting), capital, tax_payroll, finance (cards, lenders) or unknown (no default account or unambiguous distribution set in Sage). vendor_group (DEF, USD, PAY ...) is how Sage pays the vendor.
measures.ask: What do we owe suppliers right now, by aging bucket?

measures.name: Purchase order value
measures.definition: Total of purchase orders by order date, drafts left out.
measures.ask: Why did purchase order spend change last month? Which suppliers drove it?

measures.name: Purchase orders placed
measures.definition: Purchase orders by order date, one per purchase order record (two suppliers' orders that share a number count as two), drafts left out.
measures.ask: How many POs did each buyer place this quarter?

measures.name: Late purchase orders
measures.definition: Purchase orders past their promised or requested date now (the order view's verdict is late).
measures.ask: Which suppliers have the most late purchase orders right now?

measures.name: Batches produced
measures.definition: Production batches realized (made), by the date they were realized.
measures.ask: How many batches did each production line make per month this year?

measures.name: Batches on quality hold
measures.definition: Batches made (status Realized) whose quality status is On-Hold now. Unmade batches carry On-Hold by default and are not counted.
measures.ask: Which products have batches on quality hold right now?

parameters.says: made over a year ago and still marked On-Hold (holds the old systems never cleared)

measures.name: Stock on hand
measures.definition: Quantity on hand now per item, per unit of measure.
measures.ask: Which finished goods are short against open orders?

measures.name: Mail received from outside
measures.definition: Distinct emails from a domain no PLX staff address uses, addressed (to or cc) to a PLX mailbox, by received date (a message is counted once, however many mailboxes hold it).
measures.where: owner_role IN ('to', 'cc') AND sender_domain NOT IN (SELECT split_part(email, '@', 2) FROM staff WHERE email IS NOT NULL)
measures.ask: Is incoming mail unusual this week against the usual week?

measures.name: Complaints said in mail and Teams
measures.definition: Complaints a model found in mail and Teams messages (comms_findings, each checked against a quote of its message), by the time it was said.
measures.ask: What are customers complaining about most in the last 30 days?

measures.name: Requests said in mail and Teams
measures.definition: Requests a model found in mail and Teams messages (comms_findings), by the time they were said.
measures.ask: What are customers asking us for most this month?

measures.name: Decisions said in mail and Teams
measures.definition: Decisions a model found in mail and Teams messages (comms_findings), by the time they were said.
measures.ask: How many decisions were made per week lately, and by whom?

measures.name: Loss on lines sold below cost
measures.definition: Line revenue less line cost on posted sales invoice lines sold for more than 0 whose cost is above their revenue (a negative margin), by invoice date: what selling below cost lost. Not counted: lines without a cost, credit or discount lines (revenue 0 or less), and lines whose cost looks wrong (more than 5 times the line's revenue: cost_looks_wrong lists them). A line whose margin the reader may not read counts in unread_cells, never as no loss.
measures.where: margin_basis IS DISTINCT FROM 'cost_unknown' AND coalesce(revenue > 0, true) AND (margin IS NULL OR (margin < 0 AND coalesce(margin >= -4 * revenue, true)))
measures.ask: Which customers did we sell to below cost last month?

parameters.says: invoices held only in Business Central

measures.name: Invoice lines whose cost looks wrong
measures.definition: Posted sales invoice lines sold for more than 0 whose cost is more than 5 times their revenue (a cost that far off the price is most likely a wrong unit cost in Sage, such as a case cost on an each line), by invoice date. They are left out of gross_margin and loss_below_cost and listed here to be checked.
measures.ask: Which invoice lines have a cost that looks wrong?

parameters.says: invoices held only in Business Central

measures.name: Customers invoiced
measures.definition: Customers with a posted sales invoice, by invoice date, one per customer record (two accounts with one name count as two).
measures.ask: Which customers have gone quiet in the last 90 days?

parameters.says: invoices held only in Business Central

measures.name: Batches rejected by QC
measures.definition: Realized (made) batches whose quality status is Rejected, by the date they were realized.
measures.ask: How many batches were rejected this year, by product?

measures.name: Mail sent by our people
measures.definition: Distinct emails sent from a PLX staff address domain, by sent date (a message is counted once, however many mailboxes hold it); by sender for each person's mail workload.
measures.where: sender_domain IN (SELECT split_part(email, '@', 2) FROM staff WHERE email IS NOT NULL)
measures.ask: Who sent the most mail last month against the month before?

measures.name: Batch reject rate
measures.definition: Of the batches made (status Realized), by the day they were made, the percent whose quality status is Rejected (numerator: rejected realized batches; denominator: all realized batches made). Unmade batches carry On-Hold by default and are left out.
measures.ask: What is our batch reject rate this year by production line?
measures.denominator: Realized (made) batches (status = 'Realized') by realized_date, counted as distinct handles

measures.name: Batch QC hold rate
measures.definition: Of the batches made (status Realized), by the day they were made, the percent still on quality hold (numerator: realized batches with quality status On-Hold; denominator: all realized batches made). Unmade batches carry On-Hold by default and are left out.
measures.ask: What share of batches made this quarter is still on hold?
measures.denominator: Realized (made) batches (status = 'Realized') by realized_date, counted as distinct handles

measures.name: Batch yield
measures.definition: Produced quantity over planned quantity, in percent, of the batches made (status Realized) that state both with planned above 0, by the day they were made (numerator: sum of produced_quantity; denominator: sum of planned_quantity): over 100 means more was made than planned.
measures.where: status = 'Realized' AND planned_quantity > 0 AND produced_quantity IS NOT NULL
measures.ask: What is our batch yield by production line this quarter?
measures.denominator: Sum of planned_quantity on realized batches where planned_quantity > 0 and produced_quantity IS NOT NULL

measures.name: Open orders nobody is working
measures.definition: Orders the books still show open that are not live: every line states nothing left to ship, or the order is past its required date by more than closed orders take to finish with nothing ordered or invoiced in that time. Never counted as late. Reads 0 until the order view's first refresh after this rule shipped (the column does not exist before it).
measures.where: status = 'open' AND to_jsonb(sales_orders) ->> 'open_state' IN ('stale', 'nothing_outstanding') AND order_type IS DISTINCT FROM 'quote' AND of_record IS NOT NULL
measures.ask: How many open orders are stale, with nothing owed or nobody working them?

measures.name: Share of open orders that are late
measures.definition: Of the open customer orders that are still going (quotes left out; not those that owe nothing or that nobody has worked for longer than closed orders take), the percent past their required date as they stand now (numerator: open live sales orders with days_late > 0; denominator: all open live sales orders).
measures.where: status = 'open' AND coalesce(to_jsonb(sales_orders) ->> 'open_state', 'live') = 'live' AND order_type IS DISTINCT FROM 'quote' AND of_record IS NOT NULL
measures.ask: What share of open orders is late right now, per salesperson?
measures.denominator: Open live sales orders (status = 'open', open_state = 'live', excluding quotes, of_record IS NOT NULL), counted as distinct handles

measures.name: Share of receivables overdue
measures.definition: Of what customers owe (open receivable documents, net of credits), the percent past due per currency as it stands now (numerator: net open receivables with days_overdue > 0; denominator: total net open receivables, per currency).
measures.ask: What share of our receivables is overdue in each currency?
measures.denominator: Total net open receivables (sum of amount_due across all open customer_balances documents, per currency)

measures.name: Payables overdue
measures.definition: What PLX owes now on supplier documents past their due date, gross: invoices only. Credit notes, prepayments and other non-invoice documents are not netted unless the credits parameter counts them in. payee_class says who it is owed to by the GL account Sage posts the vendor's invoices to (default account, or Sage AP distribution set when no single default account is set: trade, expense, capital, tax_payroll, finance or unknown).

parameters.says: credit notes, prepayments and other non-invoice documents past due, which reduce the figure

measures.ask: What do we owe suppliers past due, by payee class?

measures.name: Ledger postings
measures.definition: Net amount of posted Sage general-ledger lines in the company currency (debits positive, credits negative), by the journal date. Year-end closing entries (Sage source type CL) are left out unless counted in. Every posting has an equal and opposite one, so across all accounts the net is zero: read it for one account (filter by account) or by account; an expense account's spend is its sum.
measures.ask: What did we post to account 41900310001 this year?

measures.name: Receipt lead time
measures.definition: Days from a purchase order's order date to the date a receipt of it was received, averaged over the receipts linked to a purchase order (Receipt.receives), by the receipt's declared date. Receipts with no purchase order linked, and receipts dated before their order, are left out and counted beside the figure.
measures.ask: How long do suppliers take from order to receipt?

parameters.says: receipts with no purchase order linked
receipts dated before their purchase order

measures.name: Assembly orders realized
measures.definition: Assembly orders (every captured assembly order, FileMaker and Portal) that carry a realized date, by that date. Production batches (batches_produced) hold the ones that have a batch record; this counts the orders.
measures.ask: How many assembly orders were realized last month?

measures.name: Shipments on time
measures.definition: Of the shipments whose sales order states a required date, the share shipped on or before it, by the declared ship date (numerator: shipments with shipped <= required_date; denominator: shipments whose sales order states a required_date).
measures.ask: What share of shipments went out on time last quarter?
measures.denominator: Shipments linked to a sales order that states a required_date (required IS NOT NULL), by declared ship date

measures.name: Quotes issued
measures.definition: Total of quotes by the day they were issued, split by status; the accepted and rejected dates say the outcome.
measures.ask: How many quotes did we win this quarter?

measures.name: Purchases by category
measures.definition: Purchase order line amounts, by the category of the item the line is for, by the line's declared date.
measures.ask: What did we buy by category this quarter?

measures.name: Threads awaiting reply per person
measures.definition: Email threads in the last 30 days where the latest message is addressed to a staff member (to, non-bulk, unreplied for over 1 day, from someone else) on a thread that person has previously written on, grouped by person and department. Runs through the reader's own email door (emails and staff).
measures.sql: WITH st AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT person_id, name, department, email FROM staff), last AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT DISTINCT ON (mailbox, thread) mailbox, thread, sender, received_at, owner_role, is_bulk, owner_replied_at FROM emails WHERE thread IS NOT NULL AND received_at >= now() - interval '30 days' AND mailbox IN (SELECT person_id FROM st) ORDER BY mailbox, thread, received_at DESC, message_id DESC), cand AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT l.mailbox, l.thread, l.sender, l.received_at FROM last l WHERE l.owner_role = 'to' AND NOT l.is_bulk AND l.owner_replied_at IS NULL AND l.received_at < now() - interval '1 day'), wrote AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT DISTINCT mailbox, thread, sender FROM emails WHERE thread = ANY (ARRAY(SELECT thread FROM cand)) AND received_at >= now() - interval '91 days') SELECT s.name AS person, s.department, count(*) AS threads_waiting, count(*) FILTER (WHERE l.received_at < now() - interval '3 days') AS waiting_over_3_days, round((max(extract(epoch FROM now() - l.received_at)) / 86400)::numeric, 1) AS oldest_days, count(*) FILTER (WHERE split_part(l.sender, '@', 2) <> split_part(s.email, '@', 2)) AS from_outside FROM cand l JOIN st s ON s.person_id = l.mailbox WHERE l.sender <> s.email AND (l.mailbox, l.thread, s.email) IN (SELECT mailbox, thread, sender FROM wrote) GROUP BY s.name, s.department ORDER BY threads_waiting DESC
measures.ask: How many email threads are awaiting reply per person right now?

measures.name: Open operational alerts per person
measures.definition: Open operational items needing attention per person, computed through the reader's door over emails, staff, sales_orders, and purchase_orders: combines unreplied threads awaiting reply (reply_owed), open late sales orders by salesperson (counted by distinct handle), and late purchase orders by purchaser (excluding BC-only pilot, counted by distinct handle).
measures.sql: WITH st AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT person_id, name, department, email FROM staff), last AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT DISTINCT ON (mailbox, thread) mailbox, thread, sender, received_at, owner_role, is_bulk, owner_replied_at FROM emails WHERE thread IS NOT NULL AND received_at >= now() - interval '30 days' AND mailbox IN (SELECT person_id FROM st) ORDER BY mailbox, thread, received_at DESC, message_id DESC), cand AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT l.mailbox, l.thread, l.sender, l.received_at FROM last l WHERE l.owner_role = 'to' AND NOT l.is_bulk AND l.owner_replied_at IS NULL AND l.received_at < now() - interval '1 day'), wrote AS MATERIALIZED (SELECT DISTINCT mailbox, thread, sender FROM emails WHERE thread = ANY (ARRAY(SELECT thread FROM cand)) AND received_at >= now() - interval '91 days'), reply AS (SELECT s.name AS person, count(*) AS n FROM cand l JOIN st s ON s.person_id = l.mailbox WHERE l.sender <> s.email AND (l.mailbox, l.thread, s.email) IN (SELECT mailbox, thread, sender FROM wrote) GROUP BY s.name), late_so AS (SELECT coalesce(nullif(salesperson, ''), '(unassigned)') AS person, count(DISTINCT handle) AS n FROM sales_orders WHERE status = 'open' AND days_late > 0 AND order_type IS DISTINCT FROM 'quote' AND of_record IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1), late_po AS (SELECT coalesce(nullif(purchaser, ''), '(unassigned)') AS person, count(DISTINCT handle) AS n FROM purchase_orders WHERE verdict = 'late' AND NOT (coalesce(source_systems, '') = 'bc') GROUP BY 1), people AS (SELECT person FROM reply UNION SELECT person FROM late_so UNION SELECT person FROM late_po) SELECT p.person, coalesce(r.n, 0) + coalesce(so.n, 0) + coalesce(po.n, 0) AS open_alerts, coalesce(r.n, 0) AS reply_owed, coalesce(so.n, 0) AS late_sales_orders, coalesce(po.n, 0) AS late_purchase_orders FROM people p LEFT JOIN reply r ON r.person = p.person LEFT JOIN late_so so ON so.person = p.person LEFT JOIN late_po po ON po.person = p.person ORDER BY open_alerts DESC, p.person
measures.ask: How many open operational alerts does each person have right now?

measures.name: Purchase order count and value by supplier
measures.definition: Purchase order count (one per purchase order handle, never raw PO number) and total order value per supplier and currency, drafts left out. Currencies are kept separate and never added across.
measures.sql: SELECT supplier, total_currency AS currency, count(DISTINCT handle) AS po_count, sum(total) AS po_value FROM purchase_orders WHERE status IS DISTINCT FROM 'draft' GROUP BY supplier, total_currency ORDER BY po_value DESC NULLS LAST, po_count DESC
measures.ask: What is our purchase order count and total value by supplier?

measures.name: Receivables open over time
measures.definition: Daily snapshot of net open accounts receivable (from ar_daily_snapshots, snapshotted daily from customer_balances), per currency, by snapshot_date, aging_bucket and document_type. Credits, receipts and prepayments are negative. Each snapshot_date is a point-in-time balance: sum across buckets/types for one day, never across multiple days.
measures.ask: How has open accounts receivable trended over time by currency and aging bucket?
